instructions: Put 16 thin wooden skewers in a baking dish of water to soak for 20 minutes.
Cut the lamb into small cubes, about 1/2 inch. Trim off any big pieces of gristle but leave the fat on.
Put the lamb in a bowl with 2 tbsp of the olive oil, the salt and the pepper and toss to coat.
Heat the broiler to high with a rack about 6 inches below it, and line a rimmed baking sheet with foil.
Thread 5 or 6 pieces of lamb onto each skewer, pushing them close together. Lay the skewers on the sheet.
Strip 1 tbsp of rosemary leaves and 1 tbsp of oregano leaves from the stems and chop them finely. Stir them into the remaining olive oil in a small bowl. Cut the lemon into wedges.
Broil the skewers for 5 minutes. Turn them over and broil for 4 to 5 minutes, until browned and a little charred at the edges.
You're cooking the lamb to 145°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check a thick piece. No thermometer? Cut into one: it should be browned all through with just a hint of pink or none.
Meanwhile, warm the flatbreads one at a time in a dry skillet over medium heat, about 20 seconds on each side.
Taste a piece of lamb. If it's flat, add a pinch of salt.
Serve the skewers on the warm flatbreads with the herb oil spooned over and the lemon wedges.
method_notes: Great British Chefs (Esra Muslu) threads small cubes of lamb shoulder and fat on thin skewers, grills them for about 10 minutes and serves them on pitta with a rosemary and oregano oil. Turkish Style Cooking uses 1 cm cubes with salt and pepper and a milk marinade of 2 to 24 hours; the milk is left out to keep it dairy-free. Neither page shows a rating, so this is a fallback lead; the lead is the GBC version without its pickled chillies and walnut dressing. Gluten-free flatbread stands in for pitta, and the list's onions are not in either source so none are added.
